node.title: Re: Retrieving a single value from a Tie::IxHash object (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Granted, the [mod://Tie::IxHash] documentation isn't quite clear on this, but the point of Perl's [doc://tie] interface is to provide variables that look like regular variables from the outside, but can act differently. [mod://Tie::IxHash] mostly behaves like a regular hash, except that it remembers the order of keys. So perhaps it's easiest to just do the following?

use Tie::IxHash; tie my %hash, 'Tie::IxHash', one => 1, two => 2; print "$hash{two}\n"; # prints "2"

Update: Another thing the documentation doesn't seem to mention is that you can use both interfaces, via [doc://tied]:

use Data::Dump; dd tied(%hash)->Indices(qw/two one/); # prints (1, 0)
